q-269507.name: Question 1
q-269507.problem: Consider the function $f:{R}^{2}\to R$ defined by $f(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{3}.$ What is the total derivative of $f$ with respect to $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]?$
q-269507.worked_solution:
The total derivative of a scalar-valued function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ with respect to a vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ is the row vector

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{1\times n}.
$$

In our case, the function 

- acts on a vector $x\in {R}^{2},$ and

- outputs a scalar $f(x)\in R$ defined by 

$$
f(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{3}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{3}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{3})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1} & 3{x}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{1\times 2}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-269507.html:
Question 1
?

Consider the function f:R2→R defined by f(x)=x12+x23. What is the total derivative of f with respect to x=[x1x2]?

a
[2x13x22]
b
[23]
c
[23]
d
[2x13x22]
e
[2x1+x23x12+3x22]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The total derivative of a scalar-valued function f:Rn→R with respect to a vector x∈Rn is the row vector dfdx=[∂f∂x1∂f∂x2⋯∂f∂xn]∈R1×n.

In our case, the function

  • acts on a vector x∈R2, and

  • outputs a scalar f(x)∈R defined by f(x)=x12+x23.

Therefore, we have
dfdx=[∂f∂x1∂f∂x2]=[∂∂x1(x12+x23)∂∂x2(x12+x23)]=[2x13x22]∈R1×2.

q-269548.name: Question 2
q-269548.problem:
Consider the vector-valued function $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{3}$ defined by

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]x.
$$

 

What is $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x},$ the total derivative of $f$ with respect to $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]?$
q-269548.worked_solution:
The total derivative of a vector-valued function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ with respect to a vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ is the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋱ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{m\times n}.
$$

In our case, writing out the function $f(x)$ where $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{2}$, we get

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

So, the total derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}\,\,\,\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂{x}_{2}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}(5{x}_{1}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}(5{x}_{1}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}(3{x}_{2}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}(3{x}_{2})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the vector-valued function f:R2→R3 defined by f(x)=[501−203]x.

What is dfdx, the total derivative of f with respect to x=[x1x2]?

a
[5−13]
b
[510]

[501−203]

[5100−23]
e
[031−250]
Submit

EXPLANATION

The total derivative of a vector-valued function f:Rn→Rm with respect to a vector x∈Rn is the m×n matrix dfdx=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋱⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn]∈Rm×n.

In our case, writing out the function f(x) where x=[x1x2]∈R2, we get f(x)=[501−203]⋅[x1x2]=[5x1x1−2x23x2].

So, the total derivative is dfdx=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2∂f3∂x1∂f3∂x2]=[∂∂x1(5x1)∂∂x2(5x1)∂∂x1(x1−2x2)∂∂x2(x1−2x2)∂∂x1(3x2)∂∂x2(3x2)]=[501−203].

q-269557.name: Question 3
q-269557.problem:
Consider the vector-valued function $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{4}$ defined by

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 2 \\ 4 & 5 \\ 6 & 5\end{aligned}]x.
$$

 

What is $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x},$ the total derivative of $f$ with respect to $x$ at ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 4\end{aligned}]?$
q-269557.worked_solution:
The total derivative of a vector-valued function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ with respect to a vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ is the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋱ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{m\times n}.
$$

In our case, writing out the function $f(x)$ where $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{2}$, we get

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 2 \\ 4 & 5 \\ 6 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} \\ 6{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

So, the total derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}\,\,\,\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂{x}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{4}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{4}}{∂{x}_{2}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}(3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}(3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}(4{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}(4{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}(6{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}(6{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 2 \\ 4 & 5 \\ 6 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Since the total derivative is a constant matrix, evaluating it at ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$ gives the same matrix.

Consider the vector-valued function f:R2→R4 defined by f(x)=[12324565]x.

What is dfdx, the total derivative of f with respect to x at x0=[44]?

a
[12326545]
b
[01644121604]
c
[32126545]
d
[01401325]
e
[12324565]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The total derivative of a vector-valued function f:Rn→Rm with respect to a vector x∈Rn is the m×n matrix dfdx=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋱⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn]∈Rm×n.

In our case, writing out the function f(x) where x=[x1x2]∈R2, we get f(x)=[12324565][x1x2]=[x1+2x23x1+2x24x1+5x26x1+5x2].

So, the total derivative is dfdx=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2∂f3∂x1∂f3∂x2∂f4∂x1∂f4∂x2]=[∂∂x1(x1+2x2)∂∂x2(x1+2x2)∂∂x1(3x1+2x2)∂∂x2(3x1+2x2)∂∂x1(4x1+5x2)∂∂x2(4x1+5x2)∂∂x1(6x1+5x2)∂∂x2(6x1+5x2)]=[12324565].

Since the total derivative is a constant matrix, evaluating it at x0=[44] gives the same matrix.
